label: lem:H0
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:H0}
		The space $(\mathcal H_{K}$, $\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal H_{K}})$ is a separable Hilbertian seminormed space in the sense of \cite[Section 1.1]{Zbl054760064}. 
		Furthermore, $[0]_K$ is a linear subspace of $\mathcal H_{K}$, and there exists a unique norm $\|\cdot\|_{\tilde{\mathcal H}_{K}}$ on the quotient space $\mathcal H_{K}/[0]_K:= \{[f]_K: f\in \mathcal H_{K}\}$ such that $\|[f]_K\|_{\tilde{\mathcal H}_{K}} = \|f\|_{\mathcal H_{K}}$ for each $f\in \mathcal H_{K}.$
		The completion of the normed space $(\mathcal H_{K}/[0]_K, \|\cdot\|_{\tilde{\mathcal H}_{K}})$ is a separable Hilbert space, denoted by $(\tilde{\mathcal H}_{K}, \|\cdot\|_{\tilde{\mathcal H}_{K}})$.

label: prop:sub_g_mmd_framework
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:sub_g_mmd_framework}
		Let $V,\Psi:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be doubling functions satisfying \eqref{eq:2doublingfunctions}.
		Let $({\mathbb X},d,m,\mathcal E,\mathcal F)$ be an MMD that admits heat kernels, satisfies $\mathrm{HKE}_{\rm full}(\Psi)$ and has volume growth profile $V$.
		Let $\mathcal L$ be the operator associated with $(\mathcal E,\mathcal F)$.
		Fix $x_0\in{\mathbb X}$ and set $h(x):=\exp(d(x_0,x))$ for $x\in{\mathbb X}$.
		Let $\gamma\geq 0$ and let $K_\gamma$ be as in \eqref{eq:K0} and \eqref{eq:Kgamma}.
		Suppose there exists $\alpha_0\in(0,1)$ such that
		\begin{itemize}
			\item if $\gamma = 0$, then 
			\[
			\Parentheses*{V\Parentheses*{\Psi^{-1}(t)}}^{-1}\lesssim t^{-\alpha_0},\qquad\text{uniformly in }t\in(0,1];
			\]
			\item else if $\gamma \neq 0$, then 
			\[
			\int_0^\infty \frac{s^\gamma}{V\Parentheses*{\Psi^{-1}(t+s)}}\,\frac{\mathrm ds}{s}\lesssim t^{-\alpha_0},\qquad\text{uniformly in }t\in(0,1].
			\]
		\end{itemize}
		Let stochastic basis $(\Omega, \mathscr{F}, (\mathscr{F}_t)_{t\geq 0}, \mathbb P, W)$, drift coefficient $b$, noise coefficient
		$\sigma$, and initial value $f$ be given as in \eqref{eq:SB}--\eqref{eq:IV} with $K$ being replaced by $K_\gamma$.
		Suppose there exists a $\mathbb P$-null subset $\mathrm N_{\ref{c:Lip}}$ of $\Omega$ such that \eqref{eq:LiG} and \eqref{ineq:g_lip} hold.
		Then, there exists a unique (up to indistinguishability) strong solution $(u_t)_{t\geq 0}$ to the SPDE \eqref{eq:spde}.
				Furthermore, if in addition \eqref{eq:con} and \eqref{cond:pos_zero} hold, then the unique strong solution satisfies the strict positivity stated in Theorem~\ref{thm:comparison}.
		In particular, for the Parabolic Anderson model
		\[
		\partial_t u = \mathcal L u + u\dot W_t,\qquad u(0,\cdot)=u_0,
		\]
		with either white noise $K_0$ or colored noise $K_\gamma$ under the respective conditions above,
		the unique strong solution satisfies
		\[
		\mathbb P\Parentheses*{u(t,x)>0\text{ for all }t>0,\;x\in{\mathbb X}}=1
		\]
		whenever $u_0\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm{tem},+}_{{\mathbb X},h}$ is not identically zero.

label: rem:sub-g-general
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:sub-g-general}
		Let \(V,\Psi : [0,\infty) \to [0,\infty)\) be doubling functions such that
		\begin{align}\label{ineq:sub_g_escape_vol_constrain}
			\frac{R^2}{r^2} \lesssim \frac{\Psi(R)}{\Psi(r)} \lesssim \frac{R\,V(R)}{r\,V(r)},\qquad\text{uniformly in } 0<r\le R.
		\end{align}
		Then there exists an unbounded (that is, infinite diameter) MMD space
		\[
		({\mathbb X},d,m,\mathcal E,\mathcal F)
		\]
		that satisfies the full sub-Gaussian kernel estimate \(\mathrm{HKE}_{\rm full}(\Psi)\), and the metric measure space $({\mathbb X},d,m)$ has volume growth profile $V$.
		By tracing the proofs in \cite{murugan2024diffusions}, one sees that the metric space $({\mathbb X},d)$ here is a complete locally compact metric space (see \cite[Proofs of Theorem 2.7  and Proposition 3.18]{murugan2024diffusions}).
		Note that the doubling property of $\Psi$ alone is weaker than the scale function definition (with two-sided exponents $\beta_1,\beta_2$) given earlier in this subsection; the two-sided polynomial bounds for $\Psi$ follow from \eqref{ineq:sub_g_escape_vol_constrain} together with the doubling property and are not assumed a priori.

label: ex:local_manifolds
title: Example
body_md:
\label{ex:local_manifolds}
 By \cite[Theorem~2.7]{hebisch2001relation}, a sufficient criterion for \eqref{eq:manifold_gaussian} consists of \eqref{eq:manifold_local_volume} and a constant $C_P>0$ such that
 \[
  \int_{B_r(x)}|v-v_{B_r(x)}|^2\,dm
  \leq C_P r^2\int_{B_r(x)}|\nabla v|^2\,dm,
  \qquad v_B:=\frac1{m(B)}\int_B v\,dm,
 \]
 for every $x\in M$, $0<r\leq1$ and $v\in C_c^\infty(M)$. This includes the following manifolds.
 \begin{enumerate}
  \item Every compact connected smooth Riemannian manifold without boundary satisfies \eqref{eq:manifold_gaussian}; see \cite[Theorem~6.1, p.~428]{saloff1992uniformly}. Here $h$ is bounded and $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{tem}}_{M,h}=C(M)$.
  \item Real hyperbolic space $\mathbb H^n$, $n\geq2$, satisfies \eqref{eq:manifold_gaussian} by \cite[Theorem~6.1, p.~428]{saloff1992uniformly}.
         \item Let $M=\mathbb R^n$, let $g_{\mathrm E}$ be the Euclidean metric, and let $g=(g_{ij})$ be a smooth Riemannian metric on $M$ such that, for some $a\geq1$,
  \begin{align}
   a^{-1}g_{\mathrm E}\leq g\leq a g_{\mathrm E}.
   \label{eq:manifold_metric_comparison}
  \end{align}
  Set
  $d=d_g,\,m(\mathrm dx)=\sqrt{\det g(x)}\mathrm dx,
   \, \mathcal L=\tfrac12\operatorname{div}_g\nabla_g$. 
    By \eqref{eq:manifold_metric_comparison}, the global parabolic Harnack inequality for $g_{\mathrm E}$ transfers to $g$ by \cite[Theorem~5.5.9, pp.~168--169]{saloff2002aspects}. Its equivalence with two-sided Gaussian heat-kernel estimates follows from \cite[Theorems~5.5.1 and~5.5.3, pp.~157--161]{saloff2002aspects}. Then \eqref{eq:manifold_gaussian} follows from \eqref{eq:manifold_metric_comparison} and the fact that $m(B_r(x))\asymp r^n$.

   \end{enumerate}

label: thm:stochastic_fubini
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{thm:stochastic_fubini}
		Suppose that $(\Omega, \mathscr{F}, (\mathscr{F}_t)_{t\geq 0}, \mathbb P, W)$ is a stochastic basis given as in \eqref{eq:SB}. 
		Let  $(E, \mathscr E, \nu)$
		be a $\sigma$-finite measure space and let $T\geq 0$. 
		Let $\mathcal P_T$ denote the restriction of $\mathcal P$ to $\Omega\times[0,T]$.
		Let $\phi:=(\phi(t,\cdot, \theta): t \ge 0, \theta \in E )$ be a predictable random field in $\mathcal H_{K}$
		such that the map
		\[
			(\omega,t,\theta)\longmapsto [\phi(\omega,t,\cdot,\theta)]_K
		\]
		is $\mathcal P_T\otimes\mathscr E$-measurable with values in $\widetilde{\mathcal H}_K$, and
		\begin{align} 
			\Norm*{\phi}_{L^1_{E} L^2_{\Omega\times[0,T]}\mathcal H_{K}}:=
			\int_{E} {\mathbb E}\left[\int_0^T \Norm*{\phi(t,\cdot, \theta)}^2_{\mathcal H_{K}} \mathrm dt\right]^{1/2} \nu(\mathrm d\theta) <\infty.
		\end{align} 
		Then, there exists a real-valued measurable function  $(\Phi_T(\omega,\theta))_{\omega\in \Omega, \theta \in E}$ on 
		$(\Omega \times E, \mathscr{F}_T \otimes \mathscr E)$ such that
		\[
		\Phi_T(\cdot, \theta)=\iint_0^T \phi(t,x,\theta)W(\mathrm dt,\mathrm dx), \quad \text{a.s.,}\quad \text{for $\nu$-almost every $\theta\in E$},
		\]
		and that
		\[
		\int_{E} \Phi_T(\cdot, \theta) \nu(\mathrm d\theta) = \iint_0^T \left( \int_{E} [\phi(t,x,\theta)]_K\,\nu(\mathrm d\theta)\right) W(\mathrm dt,\mathrm dx),\quad \text{a.s.}
		\]
		Here the inner integral on the right-hand side is a Bochner integral in $\widetilde{\mathcal H}_K$.

\label{lem:tight_tem_moment}
		Let $X$ be a real-valued random field on  $\mathbb{R}_+ \times {\mathbb X}$.
		Suppose
		that for each  $\lambda\in (0,1]$, there exists $p_0 = p_0(\lambda) \ge 2$ so that for all $p \ge p_0$, it holds uniformly in $x\in {\mathbb X}$ that
		\begin{align}
			{\mathbb E}\left[|X(0,x)|^p\right] \lesssim h(x)^{\lambda}. 
		\end{align}
		Suppose further that there exist
		$\tilde \xi_1,\tilde \xi_2 \in (0,1]$
		so that for each $T>0$, $\lambda \in (0,1]$ and $p \ge 2$,  uniformly for 
		$t,t'$ in $[0,T]$ with $|t-t'| \le 1$,
		$x \in {\mathbb X}$ and $y_1,y_2 \in B_1(x)$,
		\begin{align}\label{cond:tight_moment}
			{\mathbb E}\left[\left| X(t,y_1) - X(t',y_2) \right| ^p\right] \lesssim  \left( |t'-t|^{\tilde \xi_1} + d(y_1,y_2)^{\tilde \xi_2}\right)^p h(x)^{\lambda}.
		\end{align}
		Then,
		the random field $X$ admits a continuous modification $\tilde X$ taking values in $\mathcal C_{\mathbb R_+}\mathcal C^{\mathrm{tem}}_{{\mathbb X},h}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $(\lambda_n)_{n\in \mathbb N}$ be a sequence in $(0,1]$ such that $\lambda_n \downarrow 0$, and let $(p_n)_{n\in \mathbb N}$ be a sequence in $[2,\infty)$ such that $p_n \uparrow \infty$. 
		From \eqref{eq:MM}, we know that $\mathbb M^{f}_{\lambda_{n+1}, p_{n+1}}\subset \mathbb M^{f}_{\lambda_{n}, p_{n}}$ for each $n\in \mathbb N$.
		From Proposition \ref{prop:wellposted} for each $n\in \mathbb N$, there exists a 
		$U^{(n)}\in \mathbb M^{f}_{\lambda_n, p_n}$, unique up to  predictable modification, such that $\Phi(U^{(n)})$ is a  predictable modification of $U^{(n)}$. 
		For each $n\in \mathbb N$, since $U^{(n+1)}\in \mathbb M^{f}_{\lambda_{n+1}, p_{n+1}} \subset \mathbb M^{f}_{\lambda_{n}, p_{n}}$ and $\Phi(U^{(n+1)})$ is a  predictable modification of $U^{(n+1)}$, it follows that $U^{(n+1)}$ is a  predictable modification of $U^{(n)}$. 
		From this and induction, $U^{(n)}$ is a  predictable modification of $U:= U^{(1)}$ for each $n\in \mathbb N$. 
		
		
		For any $\lambda \in (0,1]$ and $p\geq 2$, by taking $n\in \mathbb N$ large enough such that $\lambda_n \leq \lambda$ and $p_n \geq p$, we have $U \in \mathbb M^{f}_{\lambda_{n}, p_{n}} \subset \mathbb M^{f}_{\lambda, p}$. 
		Therefore, $U \in \mathbb M^{f}$ and $[U]_{\mathrm p} = [\Phi(U)]_{\mathrm p}$.
		This proves the existence part of the desired result.
		Suppose that there is any other $U' \in \mathbb M^f$ satisfying that $[U']_{\mathrm p} = [\Phi(U')]_{\mathrm p}$, then from the fact that $\mathbb M^f \subset \mathbb M^f_{\lambda_1, p_1}$, it must hold that $[U']_{\mathrm p} = [U^{(1)}]_{\mathrm p} = [U]_{\mathrm p}$.
		This proves the uniqueness part of the desired result.

		Finally, suppose that $f\in\mathcal C^{\mathrm b}_{\mathbb X}$ and let $p\geq 2$. By Proposition~\ref{prop:wellposted} with $\lambda=0$, there exists $U_0\in\mathbb M^f_{0,p}$ such that $\Phi(U_0)$ is a predictable modification of $U_0$. Since $h\geq1$, both $U_0$ and $U$ belong to $\mathbb M^f_{1,p}$, so the uniqueness part of Proposition~\ref{prop:wellposted} with $\lambda=1$ (and the same $p$) shows that $U$ is a predictable modification of $U_0$. Hence, by Fubini's theorem, for every $x\in{\mathbb X}$, $\Norm*{U(t,x)}_{L^p_\Omega}=\Norm*{U_0(t,x)}_{L^p_\Omega}$ for $\Lambda$-a.e.\ $t\in[0,T]$, and thus $\Norm*{U}_{\mathbb M_{0,p}}=\Norm*{U_0}_{\mathbb M_{0,p}}<\infty$.

label: ineq:w_ball_reg
title: Proof
body_md:
We see from condition \eqref{ineq:ref_regular} that for each $\lambda  \ge 0$, there is $C_\lambda>0$ so that for all $x \in {\mathbb X}$,
		\begin{align}\label{ineq:w_ball_reg}
			C_\lambda h(x)^{-\lambda} \ge \sup_{z \in B_1(x)} h(z)^{-\lambda} \ge h(y)^{-\lambda},\quad \text{ for all } y \in B_1(x).
		\end{align}
			Let $\lambda, \lambda_0$ be as in \eqref{ineq:var_bound_h}. By Proposition \ref{prop:MLDP}, applied on the time interval $[0,t]$, with $R=1$ and $x_0=x$, there is $\ensuremath{C_{\ref{c:gld_4}}} = \ensuremath{C_{\ref{c:gld_4}}}(\lambda,T)>0$ so that, uniformly in $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$ and $(t,x) \in (0,T] \times {\mathbb X}$,
			\begin{align}
				{\mathbb P} \left(\sup_{(s,y) \in [0,t] \times B_1(x)} |N(s,y)|h(y)^{-\lambda } > \varepsilon \right)&\overset{\eqref{ineq:w_ball_reg}}{\le} {\mathbb P} \left( \sup_{(s,y) \in [0,t] \times B_1(x)} |N(s,y)| \cdot C_\lambda h(x)^{-\lambda}> \varepsilon \right) \\
				&\,\,\,= {\mathbb P} \left(\sup_{(s,y) \in [0,t] \times B_1(x)} |N(s,y)| > C_\lambda^{-1}h(x)^\lambda\varepsilon\right)\\
				&\,\,\,\le {\mathbb P} \left(\sup_{\substack{s,s'\in[0,t]\\y,y'\in B_1(x)}} |N(s,y)-N(s',y')| > C_\lambda^{-1}h(x)^\lambda\varepsilon\right)\\
				&\overset{\eqref{ineq:MLDP_local}}{\lesssim} \exp \left(- \ensuremath{C_{\ref{c:gld_4}}} \frac{h(x)^{\lambda_0}}{t^\alpha}\varepsilon^2\right)\\
				& \,\,\,\lesssim \varepsilon^{-2} t^\alpha \exp\left( - \frac{\ensuremath{C_{\ref{c:gld_4}}}}{2t^\alpha}\varepsilon^2\right)h(x)^{-\lambda_0},
			\end{align}
			where the assumption $N(0,y) = 0$ for all $y \in {\mathbb X}$ was used in the third line by taking $(s',y')=(0,y)$; in the last inequality we used Lemma \ref{lem:exp_ineq_elementary}, absorbed constants into the implicit constant, and used the fact $h(x) \ge 1$ for all $x \in {\mathbb X}$.
		Now let $\{x_n\}_{n \in \mathcal I}\subset {\mathbb X}$ so that  \eqref{ineq:faster_than_ms} holds.
		Then we see uniformly in $t \in [0,T]$ and $\varepsilon \in (0,1)$
		\begin{align}
			{\mathbb P} \left(\sup_{(s,x) \in   [0,t]\times {\mathbb X}}|N(s,x)|h(x)^{-\lambda} > \varepsilon \right) &= {\mathbb P} \left(\bigcup_{n \in \mathcal I} \left\{\sup_{(s,x) \in [0,t] \times B_1(x_n)}|N(s,x)|h(x)^{-\lambda} >\varepsilon  \right\}\right)\\
			&\le \sum_{n \in \mathcal I} {\mathbb P} \left(\sup_{(s,x) \in [0,t] \times B_1(x_n)}|N(s,x)|h(x)^{-\lambda} >\varepsilon  \right)\\
			&\lesssim \varepsilon^{-2} t^\alpha \sum_{n \in \mathcal I} \exp\left( - \frac{\ensuremath{C_{\ref{c:gld_4}}}}{2t^\alpha}\varepsilon^2\right)h(x_n)^{-\lambda_0}\\
			&\lesssim \varepsilon^{-2}t^\alpha \exp \left( - \frac{\ensuremath{C_{\ref{c:gld_4}}}}{2t^\alpha} \varepsilon^2 \right).
		\end{align}

For $0<r\leq1$, the sub-Markov property  gives
 \[
  1\geq\int_{B_r(x)}G_{r^2}(x,y)\,m(\mathrm dy)
  \overset{\eqref{eq:manifold_gaussian}}{\geq} c_0e^{-C_0}r^{-n}m(B_r(x)).
 \]
 For the reverse volume bound, set $a=c_0 2^{-n/2}$ and choose $A\geq\sqrt2$ such that $C_0e^{-c_0A^2}\leq a/2$. Splitting the semigroup integral over $B_{A\sqrt t}(x)$ and its complement gives, for $0<t\leq1/2$,
 \begin{align*}
	at^{-n/2}&\overset{\eqref{eq:manifold_gaussian}}{\le} G_{2t}(x,x)
	=\Parentheses*{\int_{B_{A\sqrt t}(x)}+\int_{B_{A\sqrt t}(x)^c}} G_t(x,y)^2\,m(\mathrm dy)\\
	&\leq C_0^2t^{-n}m(B_{A\sqrt t}(x))
       +\frac a2t^{-n/2}.
 \end{align*}
 Taking $t=(r/A)^2$ yields
 \[
  \frac{a}{2C_0^2A^n}r^n\leq m(B_r(x))
  \leq\frac{e^{C_0}}{c_0}r^n,
  \qquad x\in M,\quad 0<r\leq1,
 \]
 proving \eqref{eq:manifold_local_volume}.

 Conservation \eqref{eq:manifold_conservation} follows from \eqref{eq:manifold_gaussian}, \eqref{eq:manifold_local_volume} and \cite[p.~1001]{coulhon2012heat}. The volume bound \eqref{eq:manifold_volume_growth} follows from \eqref{eq:manifold_local_volume} and \cite[Section~2.3, (2.6)]{hebisch2001relation}.

 By \cite[Lemma~3.6]{hebisch2001relation} and \eqref{eq:manifold_conservation}, there are $c,C>0$ such that
 \begin{align}
  \int_{B_r(x)^c}G_t(x,y)\,m(\mathrm dy)
  \leq Ce^{-cr^2/t},\qquad x\in M,\quad 0<t\leq1,\quad r>0.
  \label{eq:manifold_gaussian_tail}
 \end{align}
 For $q=0$, \eqref{eq:manifold_exp_moment} is conservation. For $q>0$, Tonelli's theorem gives
 \begin{align*}
  \int_M G_t(x,y)e^{q d(x,y)}\,m(\mathrm dy)&=\int_M G_t(x,y)\Parentheses*{1+q\int_0^{d(x,y)}e^{qr}\,\mathrm dr}\,m(\mathrm dy)\\
  &=1+q\int_0^\infty e^{qr}
       \int_{\{y:d(x,y)>r\}}G_t(x,y)\,m(\mathrm dy)\,\mathrm dr\\
  &{\overset{\eqref{eq:manifold_gaussian_tail}}{\leq}} 1+Cq\int_0^\infty e^{qr-cr^2/t}\,\mathrm dr\\
  &\le 1+C\int_0^\infty e^{qr - cr^2}\,\mathrm dr
 \end{align*}
 which is finite and independent of $x$ and $0<t\leq1$. This proves \eqref{eq:manifold_exp_moment}.

 By \cite[pp.~1000--1001]{coulhon2012heat}, \cite[Theorem~2.3(2)]{hebisch2001relation} and the $L^\infty$-contractivity of $(P_t)$, there exist $C>0$ and $\eta\in(0,1)$ such that, for every bounded measurable $f$, $x,x'\in M$ and $t,t'\in(0,1]$,
 \[
  |P_tf(x)-P_{t'}f(x')|
  \leq C\left(\frac{d(x,x')+|t-t'|^{1/2}}{\sqrt{t\wedge t'}}\right)^\eta
       \|f\|_\infty.
 \]
 Taking the supremum over $\|f\|_\infty\leq1$ gives the same bound for $\|G_t(x,\cdot)-G_{t'}(x',\cdot)\|_{L^1_M}$ by duality. Setting $t'=t$ or $x'=x$ proves the two estimates in \eqref{eq:manifold_holder}.

label: eq:manifold_noise_bound
title: Proof
body_md:
Clearly, $K$ is a symmetric Radon measure. Applying Tonelli's theorem and $L^2$-contractivity to $|v|$ gives $v\in\mathcal H_K$ for every $v\in L^2_M$. Symmetry and the semigroup property then yield
 \[
  0\leq\|v\|_{\mathcal H_K}^2
  =\frac1{\Gamma(\gamma)}\int_0^\infty e^{-s}s^{\gamma-1}
       \|P_{s/2}v\|_{L^2_M}^2\,\mathrm ds
  \leq\|v\|_{L^2_M}^2.
 \]
 This proves non-negative definiteness and \eqref{eq:manifold_noise_contraction}. For $v(y)=G_t(x,y)h(y)^\lambda$, the Gaussian bound and \eqref{eq:manifold_exp_moment} give, uniformly for $x\in M$, $0<t\leq1$ and $0\leq\lambda\leq1$,
 \[
  \|v\|_{L^1_M}\leq C h(x)^\lambda,
  \qquad \|v\|_{L^2_M}^2\leq C t^{-n/2}h(x)^{2\lambda}.
 \]
 For $s\leq1$,
 \[
  \langle v,P_s v\rangle_{L^2_M}
  \leq\min\{\|v\|_{L^2_M}^2,\,
             \sup_{y,z}G_s(y,z)\|v\|_{L^1_M}^2\}
  \leq C h(x)^{2\lambda}(t+s)^{-n/2};
 \]
 for $s\geq1$, it is at most $C h(x)^{2\lambda}$ by the semigroup property. Since \eqref{eq:manifold_gamma} gives $\gamma>0$ and $n/2-\gamma<1$, we may fix
 \[
  \max\{0,n/2-\gamma\}<\alpha<1.
 \]
 In particular, $\gamma+\alpha-n/2>0$. For $0<t\leq1$, splitting at $s=t$ gives
 \begin{align*}
  \int_0^1s^{\gamma-1}(t+s)^{-n/2}\,\mathrm ds
  &\leq t^{-n/2}\int_0^t s^{\gamma-1}\,\mathrm ds
       +\int_t^1s^{\gamma-n/2-1}\,\mathrm ds\\
  &\leq\frac{t^{\gamma-n/2}}{\gamma}
       +t^{-\alpha}\int_t^1s^{\gamma+\alpha-n/2-1}\,\mathrm ds\\
  &\leq\left(\frac1\gamma+\frac1{\gamma+\alpha-n/2}\right)t^{-\alpha}.
 \end{align*}
 Therefore, using $1\leq t^{-\alpha}$,
 \begin{align}
  \|G_t(x,\cdot)h^\lambda\|_{\mathcal H_K}^2
  \leq C h(x)^{2\lambda}
    \left(1+\int_0^1s^{\gamma-1}(t+s)^{-n/2}\,\mathrm ds\right)
  \leq C t^{-\alpha}h(x)^{2\lambda},
  \label{eq:manifold_noise_bound}
 \end{align}
 This proves the $\mathcal H_K$ inequality in \eqref{cond:exp_hk_lamda} with $\alpha\in(0,1)$, as required. Equation~\eqref{eq:manifold_noise_contraction} and the Gaussian bound also give
 \[
  \|G_t(x,\cdot)\mathbf1_{B_\delta(x)^c}\|_{\mathcal H_K}^2
  \leq\|G_t(x,\cdot)\mathbf1_{B_\delta(x)^c}\|_{L^2_M}^2
  \leq C t^{-n/2}e^{-c\delta^2/t}\longrightarrow0,\quad t\downarrow0,
 \]
 uniformly in $x$ for each $\delta>0$, proving \eqref{cond:hk_uni_bound}.

body_md:
\label{lem:PS}
		$\mathcal C^{\mathrm{tem}}_{{\mathbb X},h}$ is a Polish space.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
It is well known that if a metric space $(\mathbb X,d)$ is a locally compact separable complete metric space, then $\mathcal C_{\mathbb X}^0$  is separable.
		Let us fix an arbitrary $x_0 \in {\mathbb X}$.
		Take $\{g_n\}_{n \in \mathbb N} \subset \mathcal C_{\mathbb X}^0$ to be a dense subset and let $\mathcal X_n$  be continuous functions with values in $[0,1]$ whose support is contained in $B_{n+1}(x_0)$ and $\mathcal X_n(x) = 1$ for all $x \in B_n(x_0)$.
		Denote $g_{n,k}:= g_n \cdot \mathcal X_k$ for each $n,k \in \mathbb N$.
		Then $\mathcal A_d:=\{g_{n,k}\}_{n,k \in \mathbb N}$ is countably dense in $\mathcal C_{\mathbb X}^0$.
		
		We first show $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{tem}}_{{\mathbb X},h}$ is Polish. Define the metric $d_\mathrm{tem}$ on $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{tem}}_{{\mathbb X},h}$ by 
		\begin{align*}
			d_\mathrm{tem}(f,g):= \sum_{n = 1}^\infty 2^{-n}\Parentheses*{1 \wedge \Norm*{f - g}_{(n^{-1})}},
		\end{align*}
		which makes it a complete metric space.
		Suppose $f \in \mathcal C^{\mathrm{tem}}_{{\mathbb X},h}$, define $f_n:= f \cdot \mathcal X_n$ for each $n \in \mathbb N$ and recall that the support of $\mathcal X_n$ is contained in $B_{n+1} := B_{n+1}(x_0)$ for some $x_0$.
		Then consider for any fixed $\ell>0$,
		\begin{align}\label{ineq:first compact approx temp}
			\lim_{n\to \infty}\| f - f_n\|_{(\ell)} = \lim_{n\to \infty}\sup_{x \in B_n^c} h(x)^{-\ell}\left| f(x)\right| \le \|f \|_{(\ell/2)}\lim_{n\to \infty} \sup_{x \in B_n^c}h(x)^{-\ell/2},
		\end{align}
		which is equal to zero by Lemma \ref{lem:ref_grow} if ${\mathbb X}$ has infinite diameter; if ${\mathbb X}$ has finite diameter, then $f_n=f$ for all large $n$.
		Now for each $n$, take $\tilde g_{n,k}\mathrel{\in} \mathcal A_d$, $k\in\mathbb N$, so that $\lim_{k \to \infty} \|f_n - \tilde g_{n,k}\|_\infty = 0$; this is possible since $f_n\in\mathcal C^0_{\mathbb X}$ and $\mathcal A_d$ is dense in $\mathcal C^0_{\mathbb X}$.
		Hence, given $\varepsilon>0$, pick $n \in \mathbb N$ large enough so that $\| f - f_n\|_{(\ell)} < \frac{\varepsilon}{2}$, and pick $k = k(n) \in \mathbb N$ large enough so that $\| f_n - \tilde g_{n,k}\|_\infty < \frac{\varepsilon}{2}$.
		Hence we obtain
		\begin{align}
			\|f - \tilde g_{n,k}\|_{(\ell)}  \le \| f- f_n\|_{(\ell)} + \|f_n - \tilde g_{n,k}\|_{(\ell)} < \frac{\varepsilon}{2} + \| f_n - \tilde g_{n,k}\|_\infty < \varepsilon.
		\end{align}
		This shows the set of functions $\mathcal A_d$ is a dense subset of $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{tem}}_{{\mathbb X},h}$.

label: lem:C_temp_density_0
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:C_temp_density_0}
		$\mathcal C^0_{\mathbb X}$ is dense in $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{tem}}_{{\mathbb X},h}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since ${\mathbb X}$ is locally compact and separable, fix an increasing sequence of compact sets $(C_n)_{n\in\mathbb{N}}$ with ${\mathbb X}=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}C_n$.
		Let $\mathcal S$ be the space of compactly supported real-valued Borel simple functions on ${\mathbb X}$, and define
		\begin{align*}
			B(f,g):=\iint_{{\mathbb X}^2}f(x)g(y)K(\mathrm dx,\mathrm dy),\qquad f,g\in\mathcal S.
		\end{align*}
		The assumptions on $K$ imply that $B$ is a symmetric non-negative definite bilinear form on $\mathcal S$, and hence satisfies the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality.

		For each $f\in\mathcal H_K$, choose $f_n\in\mathcal S$ supported in $C_n$ such that $f_n\to f$ pointwise and $|f_n|\leq|f|$.
		For $f,g\in\mathcal H_K$, Fatou's lemma and the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality applied to $|f_n|,|g_n|$ give
		\begin{align}\label{ineq:H0 mixed absolute}
			\iint_{{\mathbb X}^2}|f(x)g(y)|K(\mathrm dx,\mathrm dy)
			&\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}B(|f_n|,|g_n|)\nonumber\\
			&\leq\left(\iint_{{\mathbb X}^2}|f(x)f(y)|K(\mathrm dx,\mathrm dy)\right)^{1/2}\nonumber\\
			&\qquad\times\left(\iint_{{\mathbb X}^2}|g(x)g(y)|K(\mathrm dx,\mathrm dy)\right)^{1/2}<\infty.
		\end{align}
		Thus $\mathcal H_K$ is a vector space, and the domain and the integral formula of $B$ extend to $\mathcal H_K$.
		By dominated convergence, $B(f,f)=\lim_{n\to\infty}B(f_n,f_n)\geq0$ for every $f\in\mathcal H_K$.
		Consequently,
		\begin{align}\label{ineq:H0 Cauchy Schwarz}
			|B(f,g)|\leq B(f,f)^{1/2}B(g,g)^{1/2},\qquad f,g\in\mathcal H_K,
		\end{align}
		and $\Norm*{f}_{\mathcal H_K}=B(f,f)^{1/2}$ is a Hilbertian seminorm in the sense of \cite[Section 1.1]{Zbl054760064}.
		Moreover, since $|f-f_n|\leq2|f|$, dominated convergence also yields
		\begin{align}\label{ineq:H0 compact truncation}
			\lim_{n \to \infty}\Norm*{f-f_n}_{\mathcal H_K}^2
			\leq\lim_{n\to \infty}\iint_{{\mathbb X}^2}|f(x)-f_n(x)||f(y)-f_n(y)|K(\mathrm dx,\mathrm dy)=0.
		\end{align}

		To prove separability, for each $n\in\mathbb{N}$ let $\mu_n$ be the finite Radon measure on $C_n$ defined by $\mu_n(A):=K(A\times C_n)$ for Borel sets $A\subset C_n$.
		By the separability of $\mathcal C(C_n;\mathbb{R})$ under the uniform norm and \cite[Proposition~7.9, p.~217]{folland1999real}, choose a countable set $\mathcal D_n\subset\mathcal C(C_n;\mathbb{R})$ dense in $L^2(C_n,\mu_n)$, and extend its elements by zero outside $C_n$.
		For every bounded Borel function $\psi$ supported in $C_n$, we see by the symmetry of $K$ that
		\begin{align*}
			\Norm*{\psi}_{\mathcal H_K}^2
			&=\iint_{C_n^2}{\psi}(x)\psi(y)K(\mathrm dx,\mathrm dy)\\
			&\leq\frac12\iint_{C_n^2}\bigl(|\psi(x)|^2+|\psi(y)|^2\bigr)K(\mathrm dx,\mathrm dy)
			=\Norm*{\psi}_{L^2(C_n,\mu_n)}^2.
		\end{align*}
		Given $f\in\mathcal H_K$ and $\varepsilon>0$, first use \eqref{ineq:H0 compact truncation} to choose $n$ with $\Norm*{f-f_n}_{\mathcal H_K}<\varepsilon/2$.
		Since $f_n$ is bounded and supported in $C_n$, choose $g\in\mathcal D_n$ with $\Norm*{f_n-g}_{L^2(C_n,\mu_n)}<\varepsilon/2$.
		Applying the preceding estimate to $\psi=f_n-g$ gives
		\begin{align*}
			\Norm*{f-g}_{\mathcal H_K}
			&\leq\Norm*{f-f_n}_{\mathcal H_K}+\Norm*{f_n-g}_{\mathcal H_K}\\
			&\leq\Norm*{f-f_n}_{\mathcal H_K}+\Norm*{f_n-g}_{L^2(C_n,\mu_n)}<\varepsilon.
		\end{align*}
		Thus $\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb{N}}\mathcal D_n$ is a countable dense subset of $\mathcal H_K$.

		Finally, $[0]_K$ is a linear subspace by the seminorm properties, and \eqref{ineq:H0 Cauchy Schwarz} shows that $B$ vanishes whenever one of its arguments belongs to $[0]_K$.
		Thus
		\begin{align*}
			\langle[f]_K,[g]_K\rangle:=B(f,g)
		\end{align*}
		is a well-defined inner product on $\mathcal H_K/[0]_K$, whose induced norm is the unique norm satisfying $\Norm*{[f]_K}_{\widetilde{\mathcal H}_K}=\Norm*{f}_{\mathcal H_K}$.
		Its completion is therefore a separable Hilbert space, as asserted.

By changing $\Psi$ on a $\nu$-null subset of $E$ if necessary, we may assume that $\Psi(z,\cdot)\in\mathcal H_K$ for every $z\in E$.
		By Tonelli's theorem and \eqref{ineq:H0 Cauchy Schwarz}, we see
		\begin{align*}
			\iint_{{\mathbb X}^2}F(x)F(y)K(\mathrm dx,\mathrm dy)
			&=\int_{E}\int_{E}\iint_{{\mathbb X}^2}\Psi(z,x)\Psi(z',y)K(\mathrm dx,\mathrm dy)\nu(\mathrm dz)\nu(\mathrm dz')\\
			&\leq\int_{E}\int_{E}\Norm*{\Psi(z,\cdot)}_{\mathcal H_K}\Norm*{\Psi(z',\cdot)}_{\mathcal H_K}\nu(\mathrm dz)\nu(\mathrm dz')\\
			&=\left(\int_{E}\Norm*{\Psi(z,\cdot)}_{\mathcal H_K}\nu(\mathrm dz)\right)^2<\infty.
		\end{align*}
		Therefore, $F\in\mathcal H_K$, and taking square roots proves the desired inequality.

label: lem:poisson moment bounds
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:poisson moment bounds}
		Let \(Z\sim \operatorname{Pois}(\lambda)\), \(\lambda>0\). For every positive even integer \(p=2m\), \(m\in\mathbb{N}\),
		there exists \(C_p<\infty\) such that
		\[
		\mathbb E|Z-\lambda|^p
		\le C_p\bigl(\lambda+\lambda^{p/2}\bigr).
		\]
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let \(p=2m\) be a positive even integer. By \cite[Lemma 3.1]{privault2011generalized},
		\[
		\mathbb E[(Z-\lambda)^{2m}]
		=
		\sum_{a=0}^{2m}\lambda^a S_2(2m,a),
		\]
		where \(S_2(n,a)\) denotes the number of partitions of an \(n\)-element set into \(a\) blocks
		of size at least \(2\). Hence \(S_2(2m,a)=0\) for \(a>m\). Indeed, if there are $a$ number of sets of size at least $2$, then the total elements is at least $2a$. Hence, for each $m \in \mathbb{N}$, there exists $C_m>0$, independent of $\lambda>0$, so that 
		\[
		\mathbb E|Z-\lambda|^{2m}
		=
		\sum_{a=1}^{m}\lambda^a S_2(2m,a)
		\le C_m(\lambda+\lambda^m).
		\]
		This proves the lemma.
